title: ANS comments on OMB, NRC proposed rulemakings
summary: As the pace of growth in the nuclear industry increases, policy is picking up speed, too. Over the summer, the American Nuclear Society responded to several requests for comment in nuclear policy–related matters. In July and August, ANS published letters of response concerning the Office of Management and Budget’s “Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance,” as well as two proposed rules from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission: “Integrated Low-Level Radioactive Waste Disposal” and “Reforming and Modernizing the NRC's Radiation Protection Framework.”

title: Argonne designs molten salt–based heat exchanger with ML-based monitoring
summary: Researchers at Argonne National Laboratory have proposed a compact matrix-type heat exchanger for reactors using molten salt as a coolant, featuring an embedded hardware-software system designed to improve reliability and reduce costly interruptions. The heat exchanger is a critical component of any reactor, transferring thermal energy away from the reactor core for use, either directly or to make electricity. Reactors using molten salt for this function must be monitored for blockages caused by fluid freezing, which could result from impurity accumulation or inadequate insulation. These can slow down operations and may require urgent attention.

title: Entergy Mississippi invests in the future workforce through STEM scholarships for students attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities
summary: Entergy Mississippi is investing in the future of higher education and workforce development by awarding $20,000 in STEM scholarships to four outstanding students attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities, or HBCUs, and partner institutions across Mississippi. Source

title: Entergy New Orleans joins US Department of Energy to break ground on $2M grant-funded grid hardening project
summary: Entergy New Orleans today joined leaders from the U.S. Department of Energy to break ground on a grid-hardening project that will upgrade 94 distribution poles serving the Leonidas area and directly benefit more than 1,900 customers. Making the grid stronger means customers will experience fewer, shorter outages. Source

title: Entergy named a Top Utility in Economic Development for the 19th year in a row
summary: For the 19th consecutive year, Site Selection magazine has named Entergy a Top Utility in economic development. The communities we serve in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas continue to attract some of the nation’s most competitive and power‑intensive industries. In 2025, Entergy helped secure more than $83 million in capital investments and create approximately 7,560 new direct jobs. New and expanding facilities span advanced manufacturing, clean energy production and large‑scale industrial development, further strengthening the Gulf South region’s position as a premier location for business growth.
